archetype: LUK thief whose kit splits into three named families. Arts skills are the direct chakram attacks, and the pre-5th-job Arts skills reduce the cooldowns of Void Rush and Void Blitz. Void skills are mostly utility: Void Rush and Void Blitz put the character into Dark Sight, Void Burst grants invincibility, and from 3rd job Void skills can spawn Chakri. Hex skills are the cooldown-gated wide or special attacks, and from 3rd job they consume the Chakri to throw projectiles called Resonate. Source for the family behaviour: Grandis Library's mechanics block.

linkSkill.name: Innate Gift
linkSkill.effect: Passive damage increase plus an on-attack HP/MP regeneration window. At level 1: Damage +3%, and on attacking a 100% chance to recover 1% of Max HP/MP per second for 5 seconds, 30 second cooldown. At level 3: Damage +7% and 3% of Max HP/MP per second. The skill is explicitly not affected by cooldown resets, cooldown reduction, or buff duration increase.
linkSkill.levels: Master Level 3. The level 1 and level 3 figures above are as listed on MapleStory Wiki; Grandis Library quotes the same maxed figures. NOTE: the AyumiLove Khali page states '4/7/10%' for this link skill, which is Adele's link skill value and one of several Adele fragments left in that page's overview block - do not use AyumiLove for Khali link skill numbers.

legionEffect: Flat LUK: +10 / +20 / +40 / +80 / +100 across Legion ranks B through SSS.

vMatrix.orderingSemantics: priority[] is grouped by TIER, and tier order (PRIMARY before OTHER) is the only ranking any source states. Order WITHIN a tier is the game's boost-node index order, not a recommendation - every entry carries rankWithinTier: null to say so. Grandis Library assigns Khali exactly two tiers: its page data contains "primary":[0,1,2,3] and "other":[4,5] and no secondary array. The PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER legend rendered on the page is site-wide boilerplate shown on every class page; for Khali the SECONDARY bucket is empty.

groups: Core 2: Void Rush, Void Blitz, Hex: Chakram Split
Core 3: Hex: Chakram Fury, Hex: Chakram Sweep, Death Blossom
Core 5: Arts: Cross Cut, Arts: Dual Edge
boostNodeGroups.what: These are the game's own fixed Boost Node / Enhancement Core compositions, not anybody's recommendation. Grandis Library's nodeInfo.nodes array and MapleStory Wiki's 'V Enhancements' list give the same six groups in the same order, independently.

priority.why: Grandis Library places boost node index 0 in its primary array. Its site-wide legend defines PRIMARY as boost nodes that both unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and cover frequently used skills. Core 1 does unlock a mastery node: the page's 1st Mastery Node requires Arts: Flurry / Crescentum at Lv. 40+.
priority.consensusNote: Single source family - Grandis Library's own credits assign the boost node build to the Khali Class Discord, so this is one opinion, not two. The mastery-node unlock requirement behind it is separately confirmed on MapleStory Wiki.

priority.node: Core 2: Void Rush, Void Blitz, Hex: Chakram Split
priority.why: Boost node index 1, in Grandis Library's primary array. Unlocks the 2nd Mastery Node, whose stated requirement is Void Rush / Void Blitz / Hex: Chakram Sweep-Split-Fury at Lv. 40+.
priority.consensusNote: Single source family (Grandis Library / Khali Class Discord).

priority.node: Core 3: Hex: Chakram Fury, Hex: Chakram Sweep, Death Blossom
priority.why: Boost node index 2, in Grandis Library's primary array. Unlocks the 3rd Mastery Node (Hex: Chakram Sweep/Split/Fury plus Death Blossom at Lv. 40+). Death Blossom is a Hyper Skill active, confirmed present in Khali's hyper active list on MapleStory Wiki.
priority.consensusNote: Single source family for the tiering itself; the skill names and the mastery-core existence are separately confirmed on MapleStory Wiki.

priority.why: Boost node index 3, and index 3 is inside Grandis Library's "primary":[0,1,2,3] array. It unlocks the 4th Mastery Node, whose detail on the same page reads 'Requires Resonate / Deceiving Blade (3rd Job) enhanced with V Matrix at least Lv. 40 (before Matrix Points) to unlock'. MapleStory Wiki independently lists HEXA Resonate and HEXA Deceiving Blade as Mastery Skills. CORRECTION: an earlier version of this file filed this node as SECONDARY and said Grandis justified that by the skills not unlocking a HEXA Mastery. Grandis says the opposite on both counts.
priority.consensusNote: The tier placement is single-source (Grandis / Khali Discord), but the mastery-unlock fact that the tier rests on is confirmed independently by MapleStory Wiki, and the two sources agree exactly: four mastery nodes, the fourth being Resonate + Deceiving Blade.

priority.node: Core 5: Arts: Cross Cut, Arts: Dual Edge
priority.why: Boost node index 4, in Grandis Library's "other":[4,5] array. The site-wide legend defines OTHER as boost nodes that do not need to be upgraded or carry the least priority.
priority.consensusNote: Single source family (Grandis Library / Khali Class Discord).

priority.why: Boost node index 5, in Grandis Library's other array. Same OTHER definition.
priority.consensusNote: Single source family (Grandis Library / Khali Class Discord).

trios.trio: Trio A - Arts: Flurry (or Arts: Crescentum) + Void Rush + a third slot the two sources disagree on
trios.agreedCore: Arts: Flurry paired with Void Rush. Both independent sources put these two in the same trio.

thirdSlot.grandisLibrary: Hex: Chakram Sweep / Chakram Split / Chakram Fury

trios.labelledAs: 'Primary Trio' in Grandis Library's nodeInfo.recommended block; 'Trio #1' in mastermysty's cross-class table
trios.consensusNote: Moderate for the Flurry + Void Rush pairing, which two independent sources state. WEAK for the third slot, which is contested one slot wide - see conflicts. The mystyjl table self-reports 2024-11-21.

trios.trio: Trio B - Resonate (or Deceiving Blade) + Death Blossom + a third slot the two sources disagree on
trios.agreedCore: Resonate paired with Death Blossom. Both independent sources put these two in the same trio.
trios.labelledAs: 'Secondary Trio' in Grandis Library's nodeInfo.recommended block; 'Trio #2' in mastermysty's cross-class table
trios.consensusNote: Moderate for the Resonate + Death Blossom pairing. WEAK for the third slot. The disagreement between the two sources is exactly one swap: Grandis puts Void Blitz here and Chakram Sweep in Trio A, mystyjl does the reverse.

trioNotes.text: Grandis Library's own note on its recommended trios: 'Any combination of these skills are good but preferred from same category as you want to max primary first', and '4 Boost Nodes total are needed to reach Master Level 60 for these skills (with Matrix Points used). Nodes with the same Main Skill cannot be equipped at the same time.' That first note is the closest thing to a levelling order any source gives: max the primary trio first.

vMatrix.notes: No node LEVELLING ORDER beyond 'max the primary trio first' could be sourced - nothing public states which Khali trio to take to 60 first, or how that changes between Lv 200 and Lv 260, so no order is given here. Khali's class-specific V skills are Hex: Pandemonium, Void Burst, Arts: Astra and Resonate: Ultimatum; all four appear on BOTH MapleStory Wiki and Grandis Library. CORRECTION: an earlier version of this file claimed Grandis Library's skill preview does not show Arts: Astra and told tools to prefer the wiki list for that reason. That was wrong - Grandis carries Arts: Astra with a full stat line (MP Cost: 500, Max Enemies Hit: 8, Damage: 1000%, Number of Attacks: 6, Ancient Chakram Summoned: 3) and Arts: Astra Boost as an Upgraded Passive. The claim and the validation instruction it seeded are withdrawn. Grandis Library also renders a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' chip on this page, but that chip is site-wide boilerplate - it appears identically on other class pages, e.g. the Night Lord page - so it is evidence of a game-wide v.269 boost node change, not a Khali-specific annotation, and the pre-v.269 data is not embedded in the page.

structuralFacts.originAndAscent: Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin) is Hex: Sandstorm; Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent) is Wake the Void. MapleStory Wiki labels them Origin and Ascent in its Class-Specific HEXA Skills table; Grandis Library independently types Hex: Sandstorm as a 'Key-down Origin Skill' and Wake the Void as an 'Ascent Skill'.
structuralFacts.levelBreakpoints: Hex: Sandstorm - Lv10 Ignore Defense +20%, Lv20 Boss Damage +20%, Lv30 Ignore Defense +30% and Boss Damage +30%. Wake the Void - Lv10 Ignore Defense +10% and Boss Damage +10%, Lv20 a further Ignore Defense +10% and Boss Damage +10%, Lv30 Ignore Defense +20%.
structuralFacts.masteryCores: Ten Mastery cores across four Mastery Nodes: HEXA Arts: Flurry, HEXA Arts: Crescentum (1st node); HEXA Void Rush, HEXA Void Blitz, HEXA Hex: Chakram Split (2nd node); HEXA Hex: Chakram Fury, HEXA Hex: Chakram Sweep, HEXA Death Blossom (3rd node); HEXA Resonate, HEXA Deceiving Blade (4th node). Each node requires its boost node at V Matrix Lv. 40+ (before Matrix Points) to unlock. Grandis Library and MapleStory Wiki agree on all ten and on the four-node grouping.
structuralFacts.enhancementCores: Four HEXA Enhancement cores - Hex: Pandemonium Boost, Void Burst Boost, Arts: Astra Boost and Resonate: Ultimatum Boost - each a flat final damage boost to its 5th job skill with a jump at level 10 (Hex: Pandemonium Boost reads +11% at Lv1, +19% at Lv9, +25% at Lv10; Grandis lists the maxed value of each as +60%).
structuralFacts.sharedCores: Sol Janus with Dawn and Dusk, and Sol Hecate with Styx, Charon, Phlegethon and Pactum.
structuralFacts.consensusNote: These are structure, not priority. Two independent transcriptions of the same in-game data agree, so they are safe to compare a player's build against - but they say nothing about investment ORDER.

hexa.notes: NO HEXA INVESTMENT ORDER COULD BE SOURCED, and none is invented here. Re-verified 2026-09-12: Grandis Library's Khali page data contains a sixth.masteryCore and a sixth.skillCore block but no order, priority or ranking field of any kind. What exists and what blocks it: (1) Grandis Library hosts a Khali '6th Job' infographic at https://www.grandislibrary.com/class-infographic/khali/khali-6th-job.png, credited in the page data to the Khali Discord and dated 2026-06-25 - the most current Khali HEXA artefact found anywhere. It is a grid of roughly 165 in-game HEXA core icons each stamped with a target level, with no text labels at all, so it could not be matched to skill names and was deliberately not transcribed. It needs a human or a vision/OCR pass. (2) MapleDoro carries a second image-only variant at /infographics/khali-hexa-heroic.webp under a HEXA Guide heading with a Heroic label and no accompanying text. (3) MapleGains, a GMS-data HEXA optimizer, does not support Khali. (4) Khali has no public class Google Doc; Grandis Library's Other Resources block for Khali links only MapleStory Wiki, NamuWiki and the class Discord.

hyperStats.notes: No hyper stat priority could be sourced for Khali from any reachable source. Re-verified 2026-09-12: the Grandis Library Khali page contains no hyper stat section and no hyper stat string anywhere in its markup; the AyumiLove Khali page contains no hyper stat mention; the mastermysty cross-class node table has none; and there is no Khali class doc. Empty rather than guessed. The empty array carries ordered:false so no downstream reader can mistake absence for a ranking.

passivePicks.orderingNote: Grandis Library presents these five as a set, grouped as 'Hex - Reinforce, Guardbreak, and Boss Rush', then 'Arts - Extra Strike', then 'Void - Reinforce'. It states no take-first order, and the grouping is by skill family, not by priority. Array position is NOT a ranking.
passivePicks.why: These five are the entirety of Grandis Library's hyper.recommended string for Khali, re-read from the page on 2026-09-12. Each name is separately confirmed to exist, with its effect, on MapleStory Wiki: Hex - Reinforce (Damage +20%), Hex - Guardbreak (Ignore Defense +20%), Hex - Boss Rush (Boss Damage +20%), Arts - Extra Strike (Number of Attacks +1), Void - Reinforce (Damage +20%).
passivePicks.consensusNote: sourceCount is 1 for the RECOMMENDATION: only Grandis Library recommends a build, and its own credits assign the hyper passive build to the Khali Class Discord, so it is one opinion. MapleStory Wiki is cited only as name-and-effect authority and casts no vote. AyumiLove carries no hyper passive picks for Khali (re-checked 2026-09-12).

availablePassives.list: The full set Khali chooses from is Hex - Reinforce, Hex - Guardbreak, Hex - Boss Rush, Resonate - Range, Void - Reinforce, Void - Guardbreak, Arts - Reinforce, Arts - Spread, Arts - Extra Strike. Recorded so the five picks above can be read against the four passed over: Resonate - Range (enemy search range, no damage), Void - Guardbreak, Arts - Reinforce and Arts - Spread.
availablePassives.consensusNote: Factual list of what the game offers, transcribed identically by two sources including their level requirements.

activePicksNote.text: Khali's three hyper actives are Oblivion, Death Blossom and Divine Wrath. No reachable source ranks or recommends between them, so no pick is recorded and none is invented. Oblivion's in-game text, for reference only: resets the cooldown of Void Rush and Void Blitz, reduces the cooldown of 4th job or below Hex-type skills by 50% for 30 sec, Void/Hex Final Damage +30%, 120 sec cooldown.
activePicksNote.consensusNote: Moderate that these three ARE the actives. Nothing at all on which to take.

hyperSkills.notes: No training-versus-bossing split of the passive build was published for Khali, unlike several other classes on the same site.

bossing.consensusNote: Two separately authored sources give the same first line. Grandis Library's 'For Bossing' ability card leads with it; AyumiLove lists it as a 1st Line Inner Ability. Grandis credits its inner ability block to the Khali Class Discord; AyumiLove is outside that lineage, though its independence is inferred from separate authorship rather than proven.
Both list it. Grandis puts it in a fixed three-line bossing card; AyumiLove files it under '2nd/3rd Line Inner Ability' options rather than a fixed slot, so treat the slot as unfixed.

bossing.line: Damage to monsters inflicted with an abnormal status +8%
bossing.consensusNote: Both list it, with the same caveat about fixed slot versus option. AyumiLove's wording is 'Damage to Abnormal Status +8%'.

training.line: Meso Obtained or Item Drop Rate +20% (first line)
training.consensusNote: Both give a meso-or-drop first line for the training preset.

training.line: Meso Obtained or Item Drop Rate +15% (second line)
training.consensusNote: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. An earlier version said Grandis states this as a FIXED second line while AyumiLove only conditions it. Grandis in fact ships the +15% line with its own note: 'Depending on what's chosen as the 1st Line, choose the other for the 2nd Line' - i.e. take meso on one line and drop on the other. AyumiLove's condition ('+15% if Boss Damage is 1st Line') is a different condition, so the two agree that a second meso/drop line belongs here but disagree on what triggers it.
Grandis Library only. AyumiLove's training line set stops at the meso/drop pair and does not mention Damage to Normal Monsters.

innerAbility.notes: This is the only judgement field on Khali with genuine independent agreement, and it is the field least likely to have moved: the two sources are roughly two years and several patches apart and still line up. Date caution: the AyumiLove page is stamped 2024-09-20, before the project's 2025-01-01 preference bar, and the Grandis page footer reads GMS Ver. 269 against a v.271 target. Reliability caution on AyumiLove: its Khali overview block contains verbatim Adele leftovers (link skill 4/7/10%, 'JOB SKILLS: I: Adele -> II: Adele...'), so that page is demonstrably not fully proofed for Khali. Its inner ability block, however, is NOT boilerplate - it uses a 1st-line / 2nd-and-3rd-line structure that other AyumiLove class pages do not, so it was written for this page. Neither source states an attack speed inner ability line for Khali, and none addresses whether one is wanted; Grandis's own attack stats block lists Khali at Attack Speed 8 with Chakram Booster +2 reaching Stage 6, which is the relevant fact but not a recommendation.

gearingNotes: Facts that change gear and inner ability reasoning for Khali specifically, all from MapleStory Wiki (last edited 2026-08-25) unless noted, and all stated as facts rather than recommendations because no guide was found that draws conclusions from them. MAGIC ATT MATTERS ON GEAR: Khali carries the Flora racial passive Magic Conversion, which converts 50% of the Magic ATT on her equipment into Attack Power, excluding the weapon, with set effects not applying and the conversion capped at 20% of the weapon's base Attack Power. A planner that treats Magic ATT as dead stat for a thief will misprice Khali's gear. CRITICAL RATE: her own kit supplies Critical Rate +35% from the 2nd job passive Impulse at max, and nothing else in the 1st-4th job kit adds critical rate, so she is nowhere near self-capping and the remainder must come from links, legion, hyper stats and gear. CRITICAL DAMAGE: Impulse gives +20% and the 4th job passive Chakram Expert +23%, with Chakram Expert also giving Attack Power +42 and Chakram Mastery 71% at max. IGNORE DEFENSE AND FINAL DAMAGE FROM PASSIVES: Intuition at max reads Final Damage +28%, Ignore Defense +20%, Attack Power +30; Redemption at max reads Final Damage +35%, Ignore Defense +22%, Boss Damage +30%. The two Ignore Defense figures are quoted separately and deliberately not summed, since ignore-defense sources stack multiplicatively. ATTACK SPEED: the only persistent source inside her own kit is Chakram Booster at Chakram Attack Speed +2; Grandis Library's attack stats block puts her at Attack Speed 8 reaching Stage 6 with Booster applied. The 5th job skill Hex: Pandemonium raises attack speed by up to +3 while its realm of chaos is active, which is a temporary window rather than a standing buff. COOLDOWN IS A RESOURCE: her pre-5th-job Arts skills reduce the cooldowns of Void Rush and Void Blitz, and her Hex skills are cooldown-gated, per Grandis Library's mechanics block - which is the visible reason both sourced inner ability sets open with Chance to Skip Cooldown. DARK SIGHT: Void Rush and Void Blitz put Khali into Dark Sight, and Grandis Library publishes a tested list of boss attacks avoidable in Dark Sight on her page, credited to the Night Walker Discord.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning around extending or resetting the Innate Gift link skill
commonMistakes.detail: The skill's own description states it is not affected by effects that reset cooldowns, reduce cooldown, or increase buff duration. Its 30 second cooldown and 5 second window are fixed regardless of what else the character stacks.
commonMistakes.consensusNote: Labelled strong as a FACT, not as consensus: it is the in-game skill description reproduced on the name-authoritative wiki, not a guide author's opinion.

commonMistakes.mistake: Deprioritising the Resonate / Deceiving Blade boost node
commonMistakes.detail: Core 4 (Resonate, Deceiving Blade) is inside Grandis Library's primary array and unlocks the 4th Mastery Node, which gates HEXA Resonate and HEXA Deceiving Blade. Any guide or tool that files it below the other three is contradicted by both Grandis Library and MapleStory Wiki. This file itself made that error before 2026-09-12.

sources.what: The only public structured synthesis of Khali judgement: boost node tiering (primary [0,1,2,3] / other [4,5]), a recommended Primary and Secondary trio, hyper skill passive build, recommended inner ability split bossing versus training, attack stats, the Arts/Void/Hex mechanics explanation, link skill, legion bonus, example skill build path, a Dark Sight avoidable-attack table, full 5th and 6th job skill data, and three infographics. Its credits block reads: skill icons and animations by Ikasuu, class infographic by McCain, and inner ability plus hyper passive build plus boost nodes build by the Khali Class Discord. Carries NO hyper stat section and NO HEXA investment order.

This is the single highest-value unextracted Khali artefact.

conflicts.topic: Recommended trio composition - one slot wide
conflicts.positionA: Grandis Library's nodeInfo.recommended: 'Primary Trio' = Arts: Flurry / Crescentum + Void Rush + Hex: Chakram Sweep / Split / Fury; 'Secondary Trio' = Resonate / Deceiving Blade + Void Blitz + Death Blossom.
conflicts.positionB: mastermysty's table: Trio #1 = Flurry + Void Rush + Void Blitz; Trio #2 = Chakram Sweep + Resonate + Death Blossom.
conflicts.note: The two sources AGREE on both anchors - Flurry with Void Rush in the first trio, Resonate with Death Blossom in the second - and differ only by swapping Void Blitz and Hex: Chakram Sweep between the two trios. Position B self-reports 2024-11-21. Recorded unresolved because no third source votes, but the disagreement is narrow enough that a planner can safely assert the four agreed skills and flag only the one swapped slot.

resolvedConflicts.topic: Whether Resonate and Deceiving Blade unlock 6th job HEXA Masteries
resolvedConflicts.wasRecordedAs: A conflict between Grandis Library (said to file the node SECONDARY because those skills unlock no HEXA Mastery) and MapleStory Wiki (which lists HEXA Resonate and HEXA Deceiving Blade as Mastery Skills).
resolvedConflicts.resolution: NO CONFLICT EXISTS. Grandis Library's own page contains a '4th Mastery Node' whose detail reads 'Requires Resonate / Deceiving Blade (3rd Job) enhanced with V Matrix at least Lv. 40 (before Matrix Points) to unlock', and lists HEXA Resonate and HEXA Deceiving Blade under it. Grandis and the wiki agree exactly: four mastery nodes, the fourth being Resonate + Deceiving Blade. The conflict was an artefact of the earlier SECONDARY misfiling and has been deleted.

resolvedConflicts.topic: Boost node GROUPING said to differ between Grandis Library and mastermysty
resolvedConflicts.wasRecordedAs: A conflict between Grandis's six node groupings and mastermysty's two trios.
resolvedConflicts.resolution: CATEGORY ERROR, deleted. Grandis's nodeInfo.nodes array is the game's own fixed Boost Node / Enhancement Core compositions - MapleStory Wiki's independent 'V Enhancements' list gives the identical six groups in the identical order. It is not a recommendation and cannot conflict with one. Grandis's actual trio RECOMMENDATION lives in a separate nodeInfo.recommended field that the original research never extracted; comparing that field against mastermysty yields the one-slot-wide disagreement now recorded in conflicts.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm. A resolution pass on 2026-09-12 re-opened every cited page and settled the endgame defects.

resolved.defect: FABRICATED RELATIONSHIP - the SECONDARY tier. The file recorded 'SECONDARY tier - Node 4: Resonate, Deceiving Blade' while the cited Grandis page contains only "primary":[0,1,2,3] and "other":[4,5].
resolved.what: Re-fetched https://www.grandislibrary.com/flora/khali and confirmed the page data contains exactly "primary":[0,1,2,3] and "other":[4,5], with no secondary array (the only "secondary" key on the page is "secondary":["hexSeeker"], the secondary weapon). Node index 3 IS Resonate + Deceiving Blade, so Grandis classes it PRIMARY. Moved it to tier PRIMARY, re-labelled the six nodes by their true tiers, and added an orderingSemantics block recording that the PRIMARY/SECONDARY/OTHER legend is site-wide boilerplate whose SECONDARY bucket is empty for Khali. Added a commonMistakes entry warning against the deprioritisation this file used to ship.

resolved.defect: FABRICATED CONFLICT #1 - the file claimed Grandis justifies a SECONDARY tier on the grounds that Resonate and Deceiving Blade unlock no 6th Job HEXA Mastery, and then speculated that the Grandis rationale predates those cores.
resolved.what: Verified on the cited page that sixth.masteryCore contains a '4th Mastery Node' reading 'Requires Resonate / Deceiving Blade (3rd Job) enhanced with V Matrix at least Lv. 40 (before Matrix Points) to unlock', with HEXA Resonate and HEXA Deceiving Blade listed beneath it. Grandis and MapleStory Wiki agree completely. The conflict was deleted from conflicts[] and the reason recorded in resolvedConflicts[]. The 'Grandis predates the cores' speculation is gone.

resolved.defect: CONFLICT #2 IS A CATEGORY ERROR - it compared Grandis's boost-node groupings against mastermysty's trio recommendations as if they were the same object, and never extracted Grandis's actual nodeInfo.recommended trios.
resolved.what: Confirmed Grandis's nodes array matches MapleStory Wiki's 'V Enhancements' list exactly (six Boost Node/Enhancement Cores, same order), so it is game data and not a recommendation - moved to vMatrix.boostNodeGroups. Extracted Grandis's real recommendation: Primary Trio = Arts: Flurry/Crescentum + Void Rush + Hex: Chakram Sweep/Split/Fury, Secondary Trio = Resonate/Deceiving Blade + Void Blitz + Death Blossom. Re-read the mastermysty table's Khali section directly: Trio #1 Flurry / Void Rush / Void Blitz, Trio #2 Chakram Sweep / Resonate / Death Blossom. The two agree on Flurry+Void Rush and on Resonate+Death Blossom and differ by one swap (Void Blitz vs Chakram Sweep). vMatrix.trios now records the agreed anchors at moderate consensus and the contested slot explicitly, and conflicts[] carries the narrowed one-slot disagreement.

resolved.defect: FALSE NEGATIVE CLAIM - vMatrix.notes said 'Grandis Library's skill preview does not show Arts: Astra, so any tool validating node names should use the wiki list.'
resolved.what: The Grandis page carries Arts: Astra with a full stat line (MP Cost: 500, Max Enemies Hit: 8, Damage: 1000%, Number of Attacks: 6, Ancient Chakram Summoned: 3) and Arts: Astra Boost as an Upgraded Passive. The claim was false and the validation instruction it seeded is withdrawn; vMatrix.notes now states that all four class-specific V skills appear on both sources.

resolved.defect: SHAPE DEFECT (found during this pass, not in the original defect list) - hyperSkills.passivePicks shipped as an ordered array of five objects, and hexa.order / hyperStats.priority shipped as bare empty arrays with no flag distinguishing 'unordered' or 'unsourced' from 'ranked'.
resolved.what: Grandis states no take-first order for the five hyper passives - it groups them by skill family - so passivePicks is now an object with a picks[] list plus ordered:false and an orderingNote. hexa.order and hyperStats.priority keep their empty arrays but now carry ordered:false, sourced:false, sourceCount:0 and consensus:'none' so no downstream reader can read absence as a ranking. vMatrix.priority entries carry rankWithinTier:null for the same reason.

resolved.defect: MIS-CITATION (found during this pass) - innerAbility training second line was described as 'stated by Grandis Library as a fixed second line'.
resolved.what: Grandis ships the training card with its own note: 'Depending on what's chosen as the 1st Line, choose the other for the 2nd Line'. It is not a fixed line. The claim now states what each source actually says, and both sources' conditions are recorded separately.

clearedOnInspection: No fabricated skill or node NAMES. Every name in the file was checked against maplestorywiki.net/w/Khali/Skills fetched with a desktop UA: all 1st-4th job skills, all 9 hyper passives, all 3 hyper actives, all 4 V skills, both HEXA skill cores, all 10 Mastery cores, all 4 Enhancement cores and the Sol Janus/Sol Hecate set exist exactly as written. The HEXA breakpoints and link-skill and legion values are also exact.

Spot-re-checked on 2026-09-12 during resolution: the five hyper passive picks are exactly Grandis's hyper.recommended string; the nine available passives and their level requirements match between Grandis and the wiki; both inner ability presets match Grandis's innerAbility cards verbatim; the AyumiLove inner ability block exists and reads as quoted; Hex: Sandstorm is Origin and Wake the Void is Ascent on both sources.
contest.notesOnScope: Jobs 1-4 skill builds, skill damage coefficients, damage lines and rotations were out of scope for this pass and were left untouched. No defect in the contest list concerned them, so outOfScope is empty.

writtenNote: The five endgame sections now contain only claims re-verified against the cited pages on 2026-09-12, each carrying sources, sourceCount, consensus and verifiedAt. Three of them (hexa.order, hyperStats.priority, hyperSkills.activePicks) are deliberately EMPTY and flagged unsourced - that is a verified absence, not an unverified claim. Consensus across the file tops out at moderate: no Khali endgame claim reaches 3 independent sources, so nothing here is labelled strong except one in-game skill description quoted as fact.
